name: Slack
description: Read channels, post messages, and search workspace history from your agent.
notes: Slack's official hosted MCP server (https://mcp.slack.com/mcp) acts as the authorizing user and serves only internal or Slack Marketplace apps that have the MCP server feature enabled; workspace admins can approve and manage them. The OAuth option reaches it with confidential OAuth (the app's client ID and secret; Slack has no dynamic client registration), and the user-token option sends a user token from your own Slack app. The local option runs the third-party zencoderai stdio server with a bot token; it is not maintained by Slack and has had one release, in July 2025.

envFields.label: Team / Workspace ID
envFields.helperText: First get your [Slack URL](https://slack.com/help/articles/221769328-Locate-your-Slack-URL-or-ID#find-your-url). Then use that to get your [Workspace ID](https://slack.com/help/articles/221769328-Locate-your-Slack-URL-or-ID#find-your-workspace-or-org-id).

envFields.label: Bot token
envFields.helperText: You'll need to create or have access to a [Slack App](https://github.com/zencoderai/slack-mcp-server#slack-bot-setup) to get a Bot token.

auth.credentialHelp: In your [Slack app](https://api.slack.com/apps), turn on Slack Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server under Agents and add user token scopes such as channels:history, channels:read, chat:write, reactions:write, search:read.public, and users:read ([scopes per tool](https://docs.slack.dev/ai/slack-mcp-server/#oauth-scopes)). Install the app (an admin may need to approve it) and copy the User OAuth Token from OAuth & Permissions. Sent as Authorization: Bearer <token>.

installHint: Create a Slack app with bot token scopes channels:history, channels:read, chat:write, reactions:write, users:read, and users.profile:read, then paste its bot token below. To use Slack's official hosted MCP server instead, switch the connection method and paste a user token from a Slack app that has the Slack MCP server feature turned on.
